title: The timeline has no blue outline, and its top edge drags to make it taller or shorter
goal: User 2026-09-28: 'the editor tracks have this weird blue outline, should remove that, and make the pane vertically resizable similar to the right panel being resizable.' A blue rectangle around the transport and timeline dock is visible in audit screenshots (e.g. a Ready to try picture of the Tutorial Sample recording). Find what draws it before removing it: the AppKit keyboard focus ring on a focusable view hosting the timeline (the timeline takes keys: B, I/O, J/K/L), an accent strokeBorder (TimelineZoomBar.swift and TrimTimeline.swift stroke with accentColor), or a selection state of the dock itself.
notes: Filed from the intake window. Outline: TimelineDock's own accent strokeBorder overlay, drawn while timelineHasKeyboard && !isWatching (the timeline takes the keyboard on open), removed; keyboard routing unchanged. Resize: Sources/PhotonzCore/TimelineDockHeight.swift (floor = ruler + one sound lane + scroller strip [+ caption bar]; ceiling = 70% of window minus transport+bar; drag one for one; 0 stored = default), tested in TimelineDockHeightTests. View: Sources/Photonz/TimelineResizeEdge.swift (Divider + 14pt grab strip, resizeUpDown cursor, double-click resets), overlaid on TimelineDock's top in Edit only; height in @AppStorage timeline.height (EditorState.timelineHeightKey, forgotten by walk setup 'motion'); TimelineDock now takes windowHeight from EditorView. Harness: new windowClick step (window-posted click with click count) for the double-click; listed in walk-needs-the-mac.mjs, refused under a lock. Walk: Scripts/playtest/timeline-dock-resizes-walk.json.
acceptance: Reproduced first: a walk at Next defaults opens a recording in Edit, clicks the timeline, and photographs the dock; the report names what draws the outline

No outline or focus ring is drawn around the timeline dock in any state; keyboard focus on the timeline is still real (its keys work) and is shown, if at all, the way the mock shows it, never as a system ring

The boundary between the canvas and the timeline dock is a drag handle: hover shows the resize cursor, dragging makes the dock taller or shorter live, the canvas refits above it without jumping, with the same feel and the same handle look as the right panel's resize edge
Height is clamped (at least the transport plus one track, at most about 70% of the window), double-clicking the edge returns it to its default, and the height is remembered per user
The dock's scrollers stay in their reserved space as it resizes (see the zoom task), so nothing inside jumps
Walk drags the edge up and down and photographs short, default and tall docks, with no blue outline in any

log.note: Reproduced (timeline-dock-resizes-walk, 1-default-sc.png, Next defaults): a 1.5pt accent rectangle round the whole dock. It is TimelineDock's own overlay, strokeBorder(VideoKit.Palette.accent.opacity(0.75)) drawn while editorState.timelineHasKeyboard && !isWatching, and the timeline takes the keyboard on open, so it is on in every Edit picture. Not the AppKit focus ring (CatcherView returns nil from hitTest, never first responder), not the zoom/trim strokes. The mock (video.html) draws no focus treatment on #tlDock at all.

Adversarial pass before building: a Premiere/FCP user expects the panel boundary to drag with a resize cursor and to stay put across sessions; the risks were a live drag feeding back through a moving handle (global coordinate space fixes it), a tiny window where 70% is less than one track (the floor wins), and a chosen height taller than the tracks (kept, empty space under the add row, like Premiere). After: timeline-dock-resizes-walk at Next defaults, 25 steps ok, 6 real window captures: no outline with the keyboard on the timeline or the canvas; a real drag up 300pt grew the dock under the pointer (picture refit 99%->41%); a drag down stopped at one track (86%); a real double-click (new windowClick step) sprang it back; a drag up 150 left it mid height. Scripts/test.sh: 10477 tests passed. Left rough, not filed (below the bar): grabbing the edge's upper half hands the keyboard to the canvas; hover cursor not photographable. Filed a-walk-that-closes-a-recording-and-opens-one-aga (p1, reproduced on unchanged main: probe SIGSEGV in MainThreadMeter after closeDocument + reopen of a recording), which is why the walk does not reopen to prove the height is remembered.
